item.title: Investigation ordered into teachers’ salary stoppage as 114 staff receive pay
item.description: Radrodro says the 114 affected staff received their salaries yesterday following assistance from the Ministry of Finance. He has apologised to those affected, saying t he salary issue caused concern and disruption.
item.content:encoded:
Radrodro says the 114 affected staff received their salaries yesterday following assistance from the Ministry of Finance.

He has apologised to those affected, saying t he salary issue caused concern and disruption.

Radrodro says the Permanent Secretary for Education has been directed to investigate what happened, why it happened and where the Ministry's processes failed.

He says appropriate action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation.

Radrodro has also directed the Ministry to strengthen its internal processes to ensure salary and other staff-related matters are addressed quickly and properly.

Meanwhile, as students return for the new school term, Radrodro is urging students, teachers and parents to work together to improve academic results.

He says the term is particularly important for students preparing for the Year 8, Year 12 and Year 13 national examinations.

Radrodro is encouraging students to remain focused, take their studies seriously and make full use of the support available from their teachers and families.

He has also acknowledged teachers for continuing to support students despite the challenges they face.

The Ministry is targeting a 97 percent pass rate and says achieving this will require commitment from students, teachers, parents, school leaders and education officials.

Ministry officials will also visit schools, districts and divisions during the term to meet education stakeholders, hear their concerns and monitor programmes.

Radrodro says the Ministry's main focus remains on improving learning outcomes and giving every child the opportunity to succeed.

item.content:encoded:
From studying under a kerosene lamp in Levuka to becoming Fiji’s first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist, Dr Nanise Sikiti’s journey is one of sacrifice, resilience and determination.

Dr Sikiti will share her inspiring story on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono on Wednesday at 7pm.

Dr Sikiti will share the beginning of her journey in humble surroundings in Levuka.

She will also speak about the sacrifices she has made throughout her career, the challenges of balancing family and professional responsibilities, and the people and experiences that have shaped the woman and doctor she is today.

item.title: Fiji Labour Party opposes removal of $10,000 political donation limit
item.description: Fiji Labour Party is warning that removing the $10,000 limit on political donations could give wealthy and foreign interests greater influence over the country’s elections. The Party is strongly opposing proposed changes to electoral laws that would remove the existing cap on donations to political parties and individual candidates.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Labour Party is warning that removing the $10,000 limit on political donations could give wealthy and foreign interests greater influence over the country’s elections.

The Party is strongly opposing proposed changes to electoral laws that would remove the existing cap on donations to political parties and individual candidates.

Labour says the changes could increase the risk of undue influence, corruption and compromise electoral integrity.

The proposed amendments would also allow former Fiji citizens and non-citizens living overseas to make donations to political parties and candidates.

Labour says this is concerning, particularly as Fiji prepares for the next general election.

The proposed changes are currently before the Standing Committee on Justice, Law and Human Rights and are expected to come before Parliament when it resumes on 28th September.

Labour says the proposed changes, like the recent constitutional amendments, have been brought forward at the last minute, leaving limited time for proper public discussion and debate.

The party also acknowledges that the $10,000 donation limit had been abused by some political parties in the past, but says there was at least a level of control and accountability under the existing system.

Under the current system, political parties and candidates are required to disclose their election funding within 60 days after an election.

Labour says this means voters do not know before voting who may have financially influenced political parties or candidates.

The party also says the political playing field is already uneven ahead of the next general election.

Labour claims the three Coalition government parties — PAP, NFP and SODELPA — have received an annual grant of $325,000 since 2023 to meet expenses.

It says the grant was provided without public announcement or debate in Parliament and argues that this gives an advantage to the Coalition parties.

Labour says it has raised the issue with the Secretary-General to Parliament, the Electoral Commission and the Electoral Legislation Review Commission, but claims it has not received a response from the Secretary-General to Parliament or the Electoral Commission.

The party says removing the $10,000 donation cap could further increase the financial advantage of powerful political parties ahead of the next general election.

item.title: 9-month-old Amota and 5-year-old Ruata given new life after heart surgeries
item.description: 9-month-old Nikutapui Amota and five-year-old Martin Ruata have been given a second chance at life after undergoing life-saving heart surgeries at the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Heart Hospital Fiji. The two children from Kiribati were among 13 children who underwent open-heart surgery during the latest Gift of Life medical mission, with their mothers now looking forward to taking them home healthy.
item.content:encoded:
9-month-old Nikutapui Amota and five-year-old Martin Ruata have been given a second chance at life after undergoing life-saving heart surgeries at the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Heart Hospital Fiji.

The two children from Kiribati were among 13 children who underwent open-heart surgery during the latest Gift of Life medical mission, with their mothers now looking forward to taking them home healthy.

Amota's mother, Bwenataake Tetebano, says her son had difficulty taking fluids, including breastfeeding, and experienced shortness of breath.

She says she was very scared while her son underwent the five-hour surgery, but now sees a bright future ahead for him.

Tetebano says her family back home is looking forward to Amota's return and will celebrate his recovery with a traditional feast.

She is encouraging other mothers going through similar experiences to always pray and remain thankful.

Meanwhile, Ruata's mother, Mwangarita Tobwaia, says she was not aware that her son had a heart condition until she noticed he was having difficulty waking up after sleeping.

Tobwaia says she has seen a positive change in her son since the surgery, with his eating habits improving and him becoming more active and able to wake up on his own.

Director of the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Heart Hospital, Krupali Tappoo, says 24 medical professionals from different countries came together for the mission and worked long hours to provide life-saving treatment to the children.

Tappoo says 13 children underwent open-heart surgery, while another five underwent procedures in the catheterisation laboratory, allowing them to avoid open-heart surgery.

She says the children were from Kiribati, Solomon Islands and Fiji.

Tappoo says some children with heart conditions also suffer from low oxygen levels and repeated chest infections, which can result in frequent hospital admissions.

She has acknowledged the visiting medical teams and organisations that supported the mission, saying that while the teams volunteer their time, there are still significant costs involved, including accommodation, meals, transport, medication and medical consumables.

Meanwhile, Medica Pacifica Business Manager Ivan Lal, who also donated a plasma steriliser to the Sai Prema Foundation, says he is honoured to witness the work being carried out by the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Heart Hospital Fiji.

Lal says he has worked in the medical sector for 17 years and has seen first-hand the challenges faced by the Ministry of Health, including shortages of staff and facilities.

He describes the work being done by the Sai Prema Foundation as tremendous and says he wants to support the organisation as much as possible.

Lal has also expressed his gratitude to the visiting medical team for volunteering their time to perform the surgeries and help children in need.
